newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-PLAY STARTS AT WIMBLEDON, STOPS, STARTS AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PLAY STARTS AT WIMBLEDON, STOPS, STARTS AGAIN.

text.p: Play on the third day of Wimbledon on Wednesday, severely curtailed by rain, finally started up to six hours late.

Rain in the morning then drizzle in the afternoon thwarted players, officials and fans alike but play eventually got under way with Monica Seles taking centre court against Australia's Rachel McQuillan.

Seles raced into a 6-0 5-2 lead only for the rain to intervene again after 45 minutes, causing a further 45 minute delay. When the weather relented second-seeded Seles quickly wrapped up the match 6-0 6-2.
Weather permitting, play on outside courts on Thursday will start an hour earlier than usual at 1000GMT. Play on Centre and Number One Court will begin at 1100GMT, two hours ahead of the normal time.
Showers permitted only 16 matches to be completed on Monday's opening day, but there was a full day's play on Tuesday.
